review_items.rationale:
The accepted requirement is a successful append_notify result identifying its own proposed entry, not mandatory progress or mandatory Superseded. Public handle contract promises the entry's decided index; Superseded documentation permits uncertain failure but does not permit success for another value. I reviewed the fixed plan and harness under direct-checks/8c4dc87dc3104a0ab63e5a71d28e1a3a and the stdout/stderr and parsed monitor record for f6b6e1f52baa4f8991b6320420cee535. Compilation and the real test completed. Setup asserts three unique configured nodes, leader 1 in Accept, empty accepted/decided logs and drained link queues. This occurs before the selected request, so it does not remove the investigated overlap. Core instances are moved into real actors. The only executor adapter delegates to tokio spawn/sleep through the documented AsyncRuntime extension point. The application owns transport; one FIFO per directed link is used in both prefix and fault phase. After setup, node 1 outbound messages cannot be delivered until explicit release of 1->2; no fabricated Assignments or modified protocol messages occur. Node 2's actual tagged request reaches node 1 and produces an actual Assigned plus AcceptDecide containing 101. That old suffix cannot reach nodes 2 or 3 before their replacement decision, because every delivery uses the same link policy. The new leader is formed through public try_become_leader and real Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync interactions with nodes 2 and 3; large valid timeout configuration prevents irrelevant timer elections without replacing protocol logic. Events and outgoing channels are drained; setup asserts prerequisites rather than relying on process PASS.

The retained events correlate EntryId 43db97b7-53d4-47c6-a7b0-9cf04c2eb13a: admitted value 101; real assignment prefix length 1 in ballot number 1; old outbound delivered count 0 guaranteed by the single delivery policy; replacement Decided(202) at the origin in ballot number 2 while the target future is still pending; then the actual future returns Ok(1), and public read_decided_suffix(0) returns Decided(202). The fixed old_outbound_delivered field is a driver-policy invariant, not a separately sampled counter; inspection confirms all post-setup source-1 links are blocked until after replacement. The old acceptance diagnostic is derived from an emitted AcceptDecide inspected for value 101. The returned position is an accepted-prefix length, so k-1 is the corresponding zero-based index, matching append_tracked and core read classification. The measured value is read from the actual origin actor's core storage through a public API, not inferred from the assignment or the proposed replacement. Stable op_id correlates the single target future independently of value; exact wire EntryId additionally links admission/assignment prerequisites and is asserted in the harness. No ambiguity or parse errors appear in the retained monitor record.

The implication requires observed_value == admitted.proposed only when the independently observed future result is successful. It therefore detects 202 != 101 without treating an error, pending call, timeout or changed ballot alone as a defect. Whole-link release preserves FIFO and delivers any preceding traffic; core old-ballot rejection can protect log consistency while the runtime consumes a stale assignment. Source ordering explains the observation: record_assignment matches EntryId without current-ballot validation; until receipt the origin has no assigned ballot to supersede; afterward drain_notifiers chooses index<=decided before comparing ballots. This source-supported cause is consistent with the real-producer endpoint witness. The semantic review finds no correspondence issue in this scoped comparison; controller assessment, not this label or process PASS, owns confirmation.

Explained alternatives: EntryId correlation blocks unrelated calls but does not bind the accepted position to the value occupying it after a new ballot. The ballot-based Superseded branch works when assignment is already present and a tick observes changed promise before a replacement becomes decided; the captured repository test exercises that different schedule. New leaders may legitimately adopt the old entry, so ballot change is insufficient for violation; this check directly observes a different value instead.

formation.explanation: Proposals are buffered/forwarded or accepted by the leader. A new leader first gathers per-node Promises in its ballot, chooses highest accepted round and longest corresponding suffix, and synchronizes a prepare quorum history. In Accept, flushed local writes and qualified follower Accepted reports populate per-node prefix lengths. The leader advances decided only after an accept quorum and propagates Decide or piggybacked decision. Followers require promised ballot, phase and sequence, and storage reads classify entries below the local decided boundary for consumption.

context.explanation: Caller-driven BLE ticks select ballots; explicit takeover also invokes handle_leader. A strictly newer ballot resets leader aggregation and stores a promise. A follower Prepare may acquire newer authority, or reacquire the same ballot only during recovery. Higher promised ballots reject old messages; accept sequence gaps request recovery and outdated sequences are ignored. Recovery reloads durable context and requests Prepare. Decided StopSign seals the current log and caller starts a new instance with transferred application history.

connection.explanation: Ballot election is not a decision quorum. Promises and persisted accepted history constrain new leader formation; batching is flushed before promises, old accepted indexes are reset at a new self ballot, and phase/ballot/sequence checks qualify later support. Previously decided boundaries enter Promise metadata and selected sync. Buffered proposals are appended only after preparation and only without accepted reconfiguration; followers forward buffered proposals after sync when no StopSign exists. Same-ballot reconnect resynchronizes a peer using Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync rather than treating it as ready solely from connectivity.

formation.explanation: Proposals are buffered/forwarded or accepted by the leader. A new leader first gathers per-node Promises in its ballot, chooses highest accepted round and longest corresponding suffix, and synchronizes a prepare quorum history. In Accept, flushed local writes and qualified follower Accepted reports populate per-node prefix lengths. The leader advances decided only after an accept quorum and propagates Decide or piggybacked decision. Followers require promised ballot, phase and sequence, and storage reads classify entries below the local decided boundary for consumption.

context.explanation: Caller-driven BLE ticks select ballots; explicit takeover also invokes handle_leader. A strictly newer ballot resets leader aggregation and stores a promise. A follower Prepare may acquire newer authority, or reacquire the same ballot only during recovery. Higher promised ballots reject old messages; accept sequence gaps request recovery and outdated sequences are ignored. Recovery reloads durable context and requests Prepare. Decided StopSign seals the current log and caller starts a new instance with transferred application history.

connection.explanation: Ballot election is not a decision quorum. Promises and persisted accepted history constrain new leader formation; batching is flushed before promises, old accepted indexes are reset at a new self ballot, and phase/ballot/sequence checks qualify later support. Previously decided boundaries enter Promise metadata and selected sync. Buffered proposals are appended only after preparation and only without accepted reconfiguration; followers forward buffered proposals after sync when no StopSign exists. Same-ballot reconnect resynchronizes a peer using Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync rather than treating it as ready solely from connectivity.

items.rationale:
The accepted requirement is a successful append_notify result identifying its own proposed entry, not mandatory progress or mandatory Superseded. Public handle contract promises the entry's decided index; Superseded documentation permits uncertain failure but does not permit success for another value. I reviewed the fixed plan and harness under direct-checks/8c4dc87dc3104a0ab63e5a71d28e1a3a and the stdout/stderr and parsed monitor record for f6b6e1f52baa4f8991b6320420cee535. Compilation and the real test completed. Setup asserts three unique configured nodes, leader 1 in Accept, empty accepted/decided logs and drained link queues. This occurs before the selected request, so it does not remove the investigated overlap. Core instances are moved into real actors. The only executor adapter delegates to tokio spawn/sleep through the documented AsyncRuntime extension point. The application owns transport; one FIFO per directed link is used in both prefix and fault phase. After setup, node 1 outbound messages cannot be delivered until explicit release of 1->2; no fabricated Assignments or modified protocol messages occur. Node 2's actual tagged request reaches node 1 and produces an actual Assigned plus AcceptDecide containing 101. That old suffix cannot reach nodes 2 or 3 before their replacement decision, because every delivery uses the same link policy. The new leader is formed through public try_become_leader and real Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync interactions with nodes 2 and 3; large valid timeout configuration prevents irrelevant timer elections without replacing protocol logic. Events and outgoing channels are drained; setup asserts prerequisites rather than relying on process PASS.

The retained events correlate EntryId 43db97b7-53d4-47c6-a7b0-9cf04c2eb13a: admitted value 101; real assignment prefix length 1 in ballot number 1; old outbound delivered count 0 guaranteed by the single delivery policy; replacement Decided(202) at the origin in ballot number 2 while the target future is still pending; then the actual future returns Ok(1), and public read_decided_suffix(0) returns Decided(202). The fixed old_outbound_delivered field is a driver-policy invariant, not a separately sampled counter; inspection confirms all post-setup source-1 links are blocked until after replacement. The old acceptance diagnostic is derived from an emitted AcceptDecide inspected for value 101. The returned position is an accepted-prefix length, so k-1 is the corresponding zero-based index, matching append_tracked and core read classification. The measured value is read from the actual origin actor's core storage through a public API, not inferred from the assignment or the proposed replacement. Stable op_id correlates the single target future independently of value; exact wire EntryId additionally links admission/assignment prerequisites and is asserted in the harness. No ambiguity or parse errors appear in the retained monitor record.

The implication requires observed_value == admitted.proposed only when the independently observed future result is successful. It therefore detects 202 != 101 without treating an error, pending call, timeout or changed ballot alone as a defect. Whole-link release preserves FIFO and delivers any preceding traffic; core old-ballot rejection can protect log consistency while the runtime consumes a stale assignment. Source ordering explains the observation: record_assignment matches EntryId without current-ballot validation; until receipt the origin has no assigned ballot to supersede; afterward drain_notifiers chooses index<=decided before comparing ballots. This source-supported cause is consistent with the real-producer endpoint witness. The semantic review finds no correspondence issue in this scoped comparison; controller assessment, not this label or process PASS, owns confirmation.

Explained alternatives: EntryId correlation blocks unrelated calls but does not bind the accepted position to the value occupying it after a new ballot. The ballot-based Superseded branch works when assignment is already present and a tick observes changed promise before a replacement becomes decided; the captured repository test exercises that different schedule. New leaders may legitimately adopt the old entry, so ballot change is insufficient for violation; this check directly observes a different value instead.
items.report_title: 旧任期分配消息导致写入被错误确认
items.report_answer: 三节点同一配置中，101 的真实分配消息被延迟；新主节点随后在同一位置决定了 202。释放保持链路 FIFO 顺序的旧消息后，101 的 append_notify 返回 Ok(1)，但原节点读取到的是 Decided(202)。这验证的是客户端完成关联错误，不是两个节点决定了冲突日志。
